title: Stoicism meets Fight Club - Ohma Tokita, the Alpha male
summary: A scripted essay using Kengan Ashura's Ohma Tokita and Fight Club to define the fighting stoic: accept violence and emotions, reject comfort and possessions, stay honest and self-reliant. A true alpha leads by example and inspires others to become leaders themselves.
claims: The proper response to provocation is pride, not cowardice; always entertain the option of fighting, which then lets you choose whether to engage
To control your emotions you must first accept them, and to not be a victim of violence you must embrace it; running from fears only strengthens them
Ohma embodies the fighting stoic, a mix of machismo and Stoic principles that represents the virtuous masculinity missing from western media
Mean everything you say; no one can change your mind unless you let them, and you decide when your opinions shift
Ohma wages war on comfort (hunting his own meat, no bed or roof); the more you have the less you are, and the things you own end up owning you
Select a path and stick to it regardless of what society says is worth pursuing
If you call out hypocrites you must be tougher on yourself than on others
A true alpha keeps his place through sound decisions, care and leading by example, not terror; people should follow because they perceive benefits
Too many people have never been punched in the face; a fight shows that politeness disappears under pressure, and only someone capable of tyranny can truly be kind
Vengeance is a hedonistic expression of violence; Ohma not avenging his master is applied Stoicism
The beast exists in all of us; ideologies that deny it fail, and it must be dug up and canalized rather than buried or let loose
Men are treated as expendable, so independence is a necessity; refuse handouts because they are traps
A slave is only shackled as long as he believes he is one; a job is an exchange of services, not domination
Do not let confidence degenerate into the domineering, attention-seeking stereotype of the alpha
Accept facts about yourself, like losing a fight, without anger; know your capacities and limits
Accepting your inevitable death brings freedom; most men either live in fear of it or sink into nihilism
Alphas are not born: each leader creates 10 and 10 create 100; if you are a beta it is because you live like one
